corrections: Replaced generic airframe with independently measured 2007 normally aspirated 182T: lofted cowling and hollow cabin, two side glazing bays, OmniVision aft glazing, single-piece windshield, low swept fin, three-blade 79-inch propeller and faired fixed gear.

Uniformly scaled side/front/top handbook overlays exposed an extra aft side window, overly high wing root and aft horizontal tail; corrected all three. Checked 36-foot wing span, 29-foot length, 11-foot-8-inch stabilizer span, 9-foot wheel track and 66.5-inch wheelbase independently.

Rebuilt the NAV III / GFC700 panel against the handbook image: paired GDU displays, audio strip, three lower standby gauges, switch and breaker rows, dual yokes, black/blue/red push-pull engine controls, flap control, rudder pedals and trim pedestal. Used the earlier turbo cockpit photo only for physical depth and controls.

Added four upholstered seats with headrests, posts, rear pockets and belts, side armrests and visors; wing panel seams, rivet rows, fuel vents, left-wing landing lights and separate flight-control pivots.

Wired shared named expressions to speed tape and digits, bank/pitch, standby airspeed and three-pointer altitude, true heading, climb, 2400-RPM propeller tachometer, throttle, flap, yokes and rudder pedals. Missing speed/RPM readings hide rather than reporting zero.
reviewNotes.visual: Individually inspected four turntable views, three-quarter ground, operator, cabin and wide cabin, plus side/front/top/panel overlays. Inspected zero, 120-knot/3500-foot/2200-RPM cruise, 175-knot/12500-foot/2400-RPM upper-range and negative-altitude/missing-speed/RPM states. Opposing bank/pitch and absent pointers/tapes were checked in the rendered cockpit.
limitations: The handbook three-view is schematic: uniform length/span scale gives approximately 3.15–3.2 m fin height while the printed height is 2.8448 m. Published height, propeller diameter and clearance take precedence; visible fin, nose-wheel and propeller-hub residuals remain. The reference was not stretched to conceal this disagreement.

The handbook panel photograph has perspective and callouts. GDU bezel width provides approximate absolute scale. Panel brow, upholstery, trim pedestal connection and small switch labels remain simplified; rivet rows follow visible skin divisions rather than a manufacturing fastener map.
The selected aircraft is the normally aspirated 2007 182T with NAV III/GFC700. The secondary 2006 T182T photograph has turbo and earlier KAP140 equipment, so its avionics fit was not copied.

Live glass displays are a subset of the Garmin interface. Speed is TAS, altitude geometric world elevation (GEO FT), heading true north and tachometer normalized simulated propeller speed scaled to 2400 RPM. IAS/pressure altitude, magnetic errors, navigation, oil/fuel/electrical systems and engine governor dynamics are not simulated; unavailable systems remain blank or INOP. Standby-speed scale is a coherent approximation.

Propeller/mixture knobs, trim, cowl flaps and most switches are modeled but not interactive. Source photos and handbook pixels remain local study inputs; no source pixels or photorealistic textures are distributed.

units.heading: true north clockwise from yaw
units.rpm: normalized engine-1 speed scaled to 2400 RPM

controlReview.checks: Imported GLB control-point movement tested at positive and negative commands; all 20 aircraft pass. Cockpit pairs and all ten airplane exterior pairs visually inspected. Roll, pitch, rudder and declared pedal directions corrected; ailerons and full flap deployment corrected.
limitations: Checks cover existing bindings; Cherokee and Caravan pedal geometry is static.
Full control travel and flight response remain approximations unless independently dimensioned in the model reference notes.
This audit verifies movement; it does not upgrade legacy helicopter avionics or remove previously documented geometry limitations.
